text:
My family was denied entry to Israel after being told they could enter.
Hi everyone! I wanted to share what happened to my family yesterday in the hope that it might help someone else avoid going through the same experience.

My parents and my 14-year-old brother traveled from Romania to Israel to visit me for four days. My husband wrote them an invitation letter with teudat zheut, reasons for visiting, flight tickets, they had ETA IL, everything, really. After they landed, they were taken for separate interviews at border control.

While they were being questioned, one of the immigration officers called my husband and told him that my family would be allowed to enter this time. He also said that for any future visit they would need an invitation through Misrad HaPnim, and that my husband would be responsible for making sure they left Israel by Friday.

Because of that phone call, I called my dad to tell him the good news that they would be allowed in. My family doesn’t speak English, so I wanted to reassure him that everything was okay.

A short time later, however, everything changed. They were given a refusal of entry letter stating “prevention of illegal immigration” as the reason and were put on a flight back to Romania. My husband went in the airport and tried to see if he can do something, they send him to an office where they said they couldn’t help us.. we called every single authority that came to our minds but it was still useless.. 

I still don’t understand what happened. If the officer had already told my husband that they would be allowed to enter, why were they refused afterward? It was really frustrating.. and we cannot find the guy that did this to them, because when he called my husband, it was from an unknown number, he didn’t say his name on the phone, my parents don’t know his name and didn’t see any badge with his name and of course when we called at the airport they didn’t tell us his name. 

It was heartbreaking to see them travel such a long distance, 4 hours from their hometown to Bucharest Airport, they got 5 hours before the plane departed because there was no other option to get there a bit later, then all the way to Tel Aviv another 3 hours, 4 more hours they waited to be interviewed only to be sent back after 16 hours, without ever getting the chance to hug me or see me. It was a very painful experience…..

We’re hoping to try again in the future, but I’m terrified that the same thing could happen even if we invite them trough Misrad Hapnim. 

Has anyone been through something similar? What can I do to make sure they’ll be allowed to enter next time? Do you have any advice or experience that could help?
